messages.author: aab5b71ea67a2d4f
messages.subject: Transform feature requests
parts:
Hi everyone,

I just began to use Rattle and, yes, I already have 2 feature
requests, both related to the Transform tab.

First, it would be nice to be able to define some variable
transformations ourself. For example, for the "Rescale" type, we
could have a linear transformation "y = ax + b" where we can define
"a" and "b". Of course, implementing a way define more complex
transformation wouls also be great...

And secondly, there should be a way to retrieve the EXACT
transformation made on a variable, in order to apply the SAME
transformation on another input set. For example, if I normalize a
variable (Rescale/Recenter), what was the mean and variance used? Of
course, I can use R to find the mean and variance of the original
variable, but some other transformations are less obvious, specificly
when remapping numerical variables. Furthermore, when we use only a
sample of the data ("Sample" option in the "Data" tab), it becomes
impossible to retrieve the exact transformation's parameters.

Thanks, and keep up the good work!

Réjean

messages.author: d6c0ccf22d99409f
messages.subject: rattle possibilities
parts:
Hi Rejean and list

Welcome Rejean to the Rattle community.

On Grahams togaware page there is a Todo list.

  http://rattle.togaware.com/todo.html

It has lots of suggestions for additions for Graham to do. You will see there lots of mine too, which include some thing like you requested, one is for a macro learning repeat function, where you can capture a script and then repeat the process. Graham taught me how to go to the log window, and get the commands and then paste back into the R command window, and to just keep the routine in a text file. The trouble with this is that it can only be repeated on the same data set.

One of the difficulties is that with transformations, the variable name gets changed with each transformation, which means that when you reapply the routine, or you are applying the transformation on a scoring dataset, you also need to follow the exact sequence. Graham and I have been discussing if it is possible to have macro recorder or some type of pre-defined sequences for common transformations.

Another idea was to have a macro routine sequence for a end to end process for common data analysis, which after you select the inputs, it runs the transformations, runs the models, produces an evaluation and then scores a dataset. This is a very complex process to put into rattle, but you can see in the newer version there is a reporting feature, which uses odf and a package called Weave, which produces a basic report on your data. The suggestion is to have three type of reports, one that describes the data, one that describes the modeling, lists the  inputs and records the evaluation. The last type of report gives a summary on the scoring results.

You can see in the newer versions, there is Nolans Groups. I created the transformation to apply the theory of relativity to analytics, its a long process, but basically you have a series of characteristics which describe a measurement. Lets say you have sex type, skin colour, hair colour, eye colour, fitness level. For measurement we have blood pressure, height, weight, cholesterol. With Nolans transformations, we have you extract a subpopulation called a cohort with the common feature in a specific variable, and then transform the measurement variables in that group between 0.01 and 99.9. So for hair colour, every entity has there hair colour cohort, and within in that cohort they have a value which is their position within there cohort relative to every one else in that cohort.

Another suggestion to Graham, was to have a series of drop down boxes for a equations process. Like your suggestion, I suggested to have 5 variable drop down lists, which listed every input from the selection section. In between those 5 boxes, i wanted some basic math functions, so you could write some thing like this,

[ insert new variable name ]  =   [ Height ]  [ * ]   [ Weight]  [ / ]  [ Age ]

of course this a poor example, but its an example at least.

I have found working with Graham, and trying to test some of his changes and additions in Rattle, that he is only one person, trying to make changes in conjunction with a complex employment and family, etc. Plus I bug him on the phone almost every few days with some analytics discussion or project.

What I found most useful in getting changes in to rattle was this.

1. No idea is too silly to suggest but there are complex issues in making additions in Rattle.

2. Explain out as much as possible the suggestion.

3. If possible have a mock up, example, flow chart, or drawing to illustrate the suggestion.

4. Try by using the R user guides and the Rattle log window to create some of the R code that Graham needs to insert into Rattle to implement the suggestion.

5. If you cant R code (And I cant, I am trying to learn though) then look on the Internet for other R packages that do that function that you want in R, so then Graham has a chance to slot them into Rattle.

6 Read the todo list and if you see a suggestion there that you think you could be of benefit, some thing that you could help with if you feel you could improve on the suggestion and email it to Graham. He always likes feedback, and the more detailed the suggestion, the more idea he has on implementing it.

7 If you find an error in Rattle, please include the error message, a description of the error,  a short description of the sequence before the error, and your operating system, and a date / time on when the error occurred.

Anyway, I just wanted to share my experiences of getting changes and additions into Rattle. I am now trying to get a text mining inclusion into Rattle, so any suggestions on what type of functions and outcomes people would need in a text miner would be great.

Warm Regards and Happy Rattle Using
Tony
PS Please Note I am not a creater, programmer or attached to Rattle in any way, I am just a user with lots of suggestions !

Thanks for the suggestions. As Tony suggests - example code is always
welcome and even better, patches to Rattle are great.

I've been working on the second point lately. As you say, it is
complicated. I'm picking on a simple transform at present (Rescale
0-1) to try out the ideas. In particular I am looking to capture the
transformations into PMML. To do so I now have an internal R variable,
crs$transforms, that I aim to store the list of transforms, including
the assocaited parameters (e.g., min and max for the R01). The real
win would be in scoring new datasets that have the same schema as the
originally loaded data, and then to perform transformations
underneath. It is quite a bit of work though!

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: rattle possibilities
parts:
What I found most useful in getting changes in to rattle was this.
1. No idea is too silly to suggest but there are complex issues in making additions in Rattle.
2. Explain out as much as possible the suggestion.
3. If possible have a mock up, example, flow chart, or drawing to illustrate the suggestion."

I have an idea to put R to mainstream. R and by extension Rattle is less efficient than the expensive softwares for loading bigger files , on desktop. But if you put Rattle on a cloud computer on an Amazon EC2, you can ensure people can just upload zipped .csv files , crunch and create models and then download as much as possible, with total cost of building a model very cheap.
 
Problem with this approach called the "Ohri Framework" is we need extremely skilled and evoted open source people across multiple cutting edge domains. A partial ist is below
 

The modified Ohri Framework tries to mash the following

 

0) HTTPS rather than HTTP

1) Encryption and Compression Software for data transfer (like PGP)

2) Open source stats package like R in cloud computer (like Amazon EC2 or Rightscale  with hadoop)

3) GUI to make it easy to use (like Rattle GUI and PMML Package)

4) A Data Mining Open Source Package (like Rapid Miner or Splunk)

5) RIA Graphics (like Silverlight )

6) Secure Output to cloud computing devices (like Google Docs)

7) Billing or Priced at simple cost plus X % (where simple cost can be like 0.85 cent /per instance hour or more depending on usage and X should not be more than 15 %)

8) Open source sharing of all code to ensure community sandboxing

 

Intention is to remove fixed computing costs of servers and desktops to normal PC's (Ubuntu Linux ) with (Firefox or IE Explorer ) access to secure data mining on demand .

On tap demand mining to anyone in the world without going for the big license purchases/renewals (software expenses) or big hardware purchases (which become obsolete in 2-3 years).

 

Your views,

 

Ajay

 Ohri Framework.

messages.author: f4ac9004a21f0fed
messages.subject: Re: rattle possibilities
parts:
No. I was in touch with Zementis, and they did contribute to the PMML package in Rattle.
 
Scoring service at Zementis (as I understood) on the SaaS is simple application/deployment  of PMML model. You can not create a model (like time series ,or a decision tree or a clsuter analysis ), but if you  have a model, you can apply it .
 
Both these options  are offline as per the page.
 
Rules Engine
 Scorecards

 By putting say the RATTLE online as SaaS backed by on -demand processor, you no longer need to
 
1) Buy expensive hardware which is barely utilized for full use more than 30-40 %
 
and obsolete in 2-3 years
 
2) Hire a consultant
 
3) Pay expensive fees to softwares which are better at bigger files crunching, but acceptable and un innovative in stats algorithms compared to R.
 
Surprisingly Zementis did write back to me, but when I explained I wanted to put all RATTLE features on remote processing, did not reply back.
 
Once you have this thing done and up (painful -requires team of exceptional coders AND hadoop and encryption for free ! ) , any guy with a 200 mb file in any developing country can just use an internet connection and create a data mining/predictive analytics model for a few dollars more.
 
 
 
 
Ajay
www.decisionstats.com

On Thu, Aug 28, 2008 at 1:16 PM, Ajay ohri <ohri...@gmail.com> wrote:
No. I was in touch with Zementis, and they did contribute to the PMML package in Rattle.
 
Scoring service at Zementis (as I understood) on the SaaS is simple application/deployment  of PMML model. You can not create a model (like time series ,or a decision tree or a clsuter analysis ), but if you  have a model, you can apply it .
 
Both these options  are offline as per the page.
 
Rules Engine
 Scorecards

 By putting say the RATTLE online as SaaS backed by on -demand processor, you no longer need to
 
1) Buy expensive hardware which is barely utilized for full use more than 30-40 %
 
and obsolete in 2-3 years
 
2) Hire a consultant
 
3) Pay expensive fees to softwares which are better at bigger files crunching, but acceptable and un innovative in stats algorithms compared to R.
 
Surprisingly Zementis did write back to me, but when I explained I wanted to put all RATTLE features on remote processing, did not reply back.
 
Once you have this thing done and up (painful -requires team of exceptional coders AND hadoop and encryption for free ! ) , any guy with a 200 mb file in any developing country can just use an internet connection and create a data mining/predictive analytics model for a few dollars more.
 
 
 
 
Ajay
www.decisionstats.com

> very cheap.
>
> Problem with this approach called the "Ohri Framework" is we need extremely

> A partial ist is below
>
>
> The modified Ohri Framework tries to mash the following
>
>
>
> 0) HTTPS rather than HTTP
>
> 1) Encryption and Compression Software for data transfer (like PGP)
>
> 2) Open source stats package like R in cloud computer (like Amazon EC2 or
> Rightscale  with hadoop)
>
> 3) GUI to make it easy to use (like Rattle GUI and PMML Package)
>
> 4) A Data Mining Open Source Package (like Rapid Miner or Splunk)
>
> 5) RIA Graphics (like Silverlight )
>
> 6) Secure Output to cloud computing devices (like Google Docs)
>
> 7) Billing or Priced at simple cost plus X % (where simple cost can be like

> more than 15 %)
>
> 8) Open source sharing of all code to ensure community sandboxing
>
>
>
> Intention is to remove fixed computing costs of servers and desktops to
> normal PC's (Ubuntu Linux ) with (Firefox or IE Explorer ) access to secure
> data mining on demand .
>
> On tap demand mining to anyone in the world without going for the big
